correctness.rationale: Diagonalizing the 2×2 surplus equations into sum and contrast gives the four assigned-indicator solutions and makes the feasibility test exhaustive. The inverse is entrywise nonnegative, so fewer distress indicators raise values. Both-high is maximal solvent; both-low is uniquely both insolvent. For one low firm the all-solvent candidate is feasible iff A>B and c≥B/A. Before then the low firm cannot be solvent in any candidate; the single-default candidate is feasible iff F(c)≥0 and dominates both-default if available. If F<0 both-default is feasible and unique, since both valuations fall below threshold. Convexity with opposite endpoint signs isolates one root; F(B/A)=(B/A)(βcrit−β), giving the strict interval condition and, at equality, no two-default band. Fixed marginals give event weights (1−2p+q,p−q,p−q,q), with max(0,2p−1)≤q≤p and 0<p<1. The affine slope is 2p(1−p)(1−d), including one-sided endpoint interpretation; the rational example's lowest possible value bound is 1/470 on the stated c interval.
residual_risks: The frozen marker describes exact checks, but two ancillary numerical root-location assertions in the bundled verifier use float sqrt; the proof and independent identities do not rely on them.

value.rationale: The normalized integration path keeps the symmetric no-shock valuation fixed. Along that controlled comparison the exact condition for a distress interval separates no effect, negative effect and positive effect of correlation, and the positive-valuation example rules out negative book value as a necessary artifact. This supplies a transparent analytic benchmark distinguishing conditional contagion from direct joint shocks, beyond a single numerical witness.
residual_risks: Not a policy or empirical prediction; scope is two firms, binary shocks and expected count rather than loss quantiles.
